routeInterpretation: The sampled central approach is about one-third shorter in distance than either flank, not one-third faster in measured time. Living enemies and ordinary resources were retained. Continuous movement avoided damage on the three sampled ascents; that does not imply equal safety. The separately reproduced model hesitation probe took 30 damage over five seconds on the open stair and zero at the gallery observation position. These are generated-input and model observations, not a human pacing, preference or universal-balance study.

revealingFailureAndRepair.cause: The first bell arrow correctly hit and killed the relocated watcher, ID 4. It did not pass through to the bell. The old one-shot browser expectation then waited for a target hit that had not happened. The native candidate chapter run failed the same expectation. Neither failed chapter run is counted as a complete pass.
revealingFailureAndRepair.repair: Test-only correction: record a real resolved shot, require watcher 4 was killed without activating a target before allowing a second ordinary draw, then require the bell, complete service return, persisted gate and ordinary one-time chapter outcome. No runtime, collision, enemy, health, resources, progress or save assignment was changed to pass.
revealingFailureAndRepair.successfulShotTrace: The final public run recorded the first Standard arrow killing watcher 4 with bellRung false. The second Standard arrow hit target 0 and rang the bell. The player took 18 damage between draws, retaining real combat consequences.
revealingFailureAndRepair.earlierFindings: design-observations.json and recovery-20260916.json retain the stale v1 preview expectation, incomplete intermediate metadata assembly, blocked local loopback browser attempt and historical pending-at-creation evidence. They are not rewritten into successes.

implementedScope: One bounded improvement within the existing seven-place Returning Bell: 2.8-metre central stair, shared screen/shot aperture, ordinary-arrow brass release, existing watcher relocation, retained reversible gallery control and independent flank, alternate signal-shot completion and version-correct AR inspection. No new rooms, enemies, pickups or second authored chapter.
preservation: hollow-dominions-1 and returning-bell-1 remain immutable; fresh expeditions use returning-bell-2. Checkpoints reconstruct mechanism geometry before validating the supported saved position. Old profile/envelope keys, reward receipts, controls, licenses and sibling work remain. Down D-pad selects Blink, left cycles usable damage arrows; menu/quiver priority is retained.
evidenceBoundaries: Actual production WebGL with generated keyboard/Xbox input and simulated WebXR controller poses and hand joints. No acceptance by assigned player coordinates, enemy health, resources or objective progress. First-person VR shares the chapter; AR is paused discovery-limited inspection. No hand-only archery, room scanning, physical surface anchor or furniture occlusion is claimed.
openGates: Physical Quest 3 and Xbox testing, tracking and passthrough legibility, seated/standing reach, sustained performance, comfort, unfamiliar/repeat-player comprehension, finished art/audio and the next authored chapter remain open.
nextOpportunity: Observe whether unfamiliar players notice the release and predict exposure, recover after a missed or blocked approach, and use the learned shot angle intentionally on replay. Tune this relationship before expanding the campaign. Continue under V52/V57/V76 with V65 compatibility and V68 release evidence; preserve original roadmap statuses and broader acceptance gates.
receiptScope: This final recovery adds only the nested publication record. Production files, level geometry, controls, saves, release metadata and workbook are unchanged from the publicly verified 0.15.0 runtime. This is evidence closure, not another gameplay release.
